deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated parts.

(A) Geographic table, continued from the previous page. It gives city, latitude (deg.min.sec) and longitude (deg.min.sec). The longitudes are evidently counted east of Ferro, as on the previous page (Göttingen 27°34', Greenwich 17°41'). Entries: Erfurt 51°6'0'' / 27°55'0''; Breslau 51°3'0'' / 34°49'0''; Jena 51°2'0'' / 29°34'15''; Cölln (Cologne) 50°55'0'' / 24°45'0''; Prag 50°4'30'' / 32°25'0''; Frankfurt a. Main 50°6'0'' / 26°15'0''. This is copied reference data, not computation. The values are typical 18th-century figures. Several latitudes are a few minutes too high: Erfurt is actually about 50°59', Jena about 50°56'.

(B) Transformation of a definite integral.

Goal: I = ∫_0^∞ x^m dx / (1+x^n)^{p/n}.

1. Substitution: put (1+x^n)^{1/n} = 1/y, i.e. y = (1+x^n)^{-1/n}. Then x=0 gives y=1 and x=∞ gives y=0, and the integrand becomes y^p x^m dx.

2. Differentiating 1+x^n = y^{-n} gives n x^{n-1} dx = -n y^{-n-1} dy. Hence x^{n-1} dx = -dy / y^{n+1}. Gauss first wrote factors n and then struck them out, since they cancel.

3. Therefore y^p x^m dx = y^p x^{m-n+1} · x^{n-1} dx = -y^{p-n-1} dy / x^{n-m-1}. The minus sign is dropped tacitly; it is absorbed by reversing the limits 1→0 into 0→1 (my remark).

4. Since x^n = y^{-n} - 1, we have x^{m+1-n} = (1/y^n - 1)^{(m+1-n)/n}. The integrand becomes y^{p-n-1} (y^{-n}-1)^{(m+1-n)/n} dy.

5. Factor out y^{-n}: (y^{-n}-1)^{(m+1-n)/n} = y^{-(m+1-n)} (1-y^n)^{(m+1-n)/n}. The power of y becomes p-n-1-(m+1-n) = p-m-2. Hence
   I = ∫_0^1 (1-y^n)^{(m+1-n)/n} y^{p-m-2} dy.

6. 'hinc': replace m by m-1. This gives
   ∫_0^∞ x^{m-1} dx/(1+x^n)^{p/n} = ∫_0^1 y^{p-m-1} dy / (1-y^n)^{(n-m)/n}.

7. Notation. Define [m,p] = ∫_0^∞ x^{m-1} dx/(1+x^n)^{p:n} and (a,b) = ∫_0^1 y^{a-1} dy/(1-y^n)^{b:n}, with n fixed. Then the result reads [m,p] = (p-m, n-m). Both sides equal (1/n) B(m/n, (p-m)/n).

8. Inversion, i.e. expressing (t,u) as a bracket. Gauss struck out two attempts ('t+u+n', '[t+n, t+n+u]') and wrote above them [n-t, u-t+n] = (t,u). Solving t = p-m and u = n-m actually gives m = n-u and p = t+n-u. So the correct inversion is [n-u, t-u+n] = (t,u). The written version has t and u interchanged; see errors.

Purpose: this reduces the infinite-range integrals ∫_0^∞ x^{m-1}(1+x^n)^{-p/n} dx to Euler's finite integrals ∫_0^1 y^{a-1}(1-y^n)^{-b/n} dy (Beta-function integrals). It belongs to Gauss's study of Euler-type integrals and their relations, in the circle of the lemniscatic integrals and Gamma-function notation.
errors: In the third integral line the exponent of y should be p-n-1. The next line correctly has y^{p-n-1}. The image is ambiguous and may read p-m-1, which would be a slip.
The minus sign from x^{n-1}dx = -dy/y^{n+1} is silently dropped. This is legitimate only because the limits x:0→∞ correspond to y:1→0 and are reversed; Gauss does not write the limits on the y-side.

Final inversion: with [m,p] = (p-m, n-m) one gets (t,u) = [n-u, t-u+n], not [n-t, u-t+n]. The written formula interchanges t and u, so it would assert (u,t) = (t,u). That is false for the asymmetric symbol (a,b) = ∫_0^1 y^{a-1}(1-y^n)^{-b/n} dy = (1/n)B(a/n, 1-b/n). The line is visibly a corrected, unfinished attempt (two struck-out versions).

Several tabulated latitudes are slightly off compared with modern values (Erfurt about 50°59', Jena about 50°56', Breslau about 51°07'). This is typical of the era's source tables and not Gauss's error.

results.what: Substitution y = (1+x^n)^{-1/n} transforming ∫_0^∞ x^{m-1}(1+x^n)^{-p/n} dx into ∫_0^1 y^{p-m-1}(1-y^n)^{(m-n)/n} dy
results.modern_name: Reduction of an integral over (0,∞) to the Beta integral; B(a,b) = ∫_0^∞ t^{a-1}(1+t)^{-a-b} dt = ∫_0^1 s^{a-1}(1-s)^{b-1} ds
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (1730s–1770s, integrals of the form ∫x^{m-1}dx/(1-x^n)^{...}); Legendre (Exercices, 1811–17) systematized it

results.what: Bracket notations [m,p] and (a,b) for families of definite integrals with fixed n, and the identity [m,p] = (p-m, n-m)
results.modern_name: Euler's notation (p/q) for ∫_0^1 x^{p-1}(1-x^n)^{(q-n)/n} dx and its relation to Beta values; (1/n)B(m/n,(p-m)/n)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (Institutiones calculi integralis, and papers on (p/q) integrals); Gauss used such symbols in his Gamma-function work (1812)

results.what: Table of geographic latitudes and longitudes (from Ferro) of European cities

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary substitution reducing an infinite integral to Euler's Beta-type integral, with Euler-style bracket notation. It is standard material from Euler's work, well within what Gauss is known to have handled, from his early lemniscate studies to the 1812 Gamma-function paper. The city table is copied reference data. The only noteworthy features are the private notation and a slip in the final inversion.

checkable.asserts: The 'hinc' identity ∫_0^∞ x^{m-1}(1+x^n)^{-p/n}dx = ∫_0^1 y^{p-m-1}(1-y^n)^{-(n-m)/n}dy for n=3, m=1, p=5 (difference ≈ 0).
The intermediate result ∫_0^∞ x^m(1+x^n)^{-p/n}dx = ∫_0^1 (1-y^n)^{(m+1-n)/n} y^{p-m-2} dy for n=4, m=2, p=7.
With x = (y^{-n}-1)^{1/n}, x^{n-1} dx/dy = -1/y^{n+1} (expression simplifies to 0).
[m,p] = (1/n) B(m/n,(p-m)/n), the closed form of both sides of [m,p] = (p-m, n-m).

checkable.sympy: n=5; t,u=Rational(3),Rational(1); br=lambda m,p: beta(Rational(m)/n,Rational(p-m)/n)/n; pa=lambda a,b: beta(Rational(a)/n,1-Rational(b)/n)/n; (N(br(n-u,t-u+n)-pa(t,u)), N(br(n-t,u-t+n)-pa(t,u)))
checkable.asserts: The corrected inversion [n-u, t-u+n] = (t,u) holds (first value 0), while Gauss's written [n-t, u-t+n] = (t,u) fails (second value nonzero).

transcription_corrections: Line 3: in '[-n-] x^{n-1} dx = -[-n-]dy/[-n-] y^{n+1}' the struck-out symbols are factors n, which cancel. The intended surviving equation is x^{n-1} dx = -dy / y^{n+1}.
Line 4: the struck-out prefactor is n/n (cancelled). The exponent of y should be read as p-n-1, although the hand is ambiguous between m and n.
'hinc' line: the left numerator is x^{m-1} dx; the machine's 'm-r-1' should read 'm-1'.

Final line: the uncrossed bracket written above the struck-out text reads [n-t, u-t+n] = (t,u). The struck-out fragments are 't+u+n' and '[t+n, t+n+u]'. In '[m,p] = (p-m, n-m)' both entries of the round bracket carry overlines (vincula).
